sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Online Retail of Desktop 3D Printers and Resin Filaments

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Latin notarial tradition; governed by the Código de Comercio, Decreto 410 de 1971, and Ley 1258 de 2008 for Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Colombia–Spain Double Taxation Agreement and Investment Protection Protocols
Andean Community Framework (Decision 578 on International Investment and Trade in Services)
Pacific Alliance Additional Protocol with Mexico, Chile, and Peru

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 526 de 1999 (UIAF creation); Ley 1121 de 2006 (AML/CFT prevention rules); Ley 599 de 2000, Código Penal, Articles 323-325 (money laundering and financing of terrorism); Decreto 830 de 2021 (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales); DIAN Resolución 000164 de 2021 (UBO filing requirements); Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia Circular Básica Jurídica (Part S, as updated); Ley 1258 de 2008 (S.A.S. incorporation and corporate governance).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Good Standing of the foreign parent company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies Registry or equivalent commercial registrar in the foreign shareholder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Colombia being a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention; consular legalization is not required for apostille-member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarially certified copies of ultimate beneficial owner passports
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's country of residence or passport-issuing authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for incorporation granted to the Colombian legal representative or counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Company board resolution authorizing the incorporation of the Colombia S.A.S.
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign parent company board of directors

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial owner declaration and PEP status affidavit
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ultimate beneficial owner and notary public or Colombian consular officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian consular legalization where apostille is unavailable

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and UBOs against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council sanctions list, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UIAF PEP database, Colombian criminal records and judicial arrest warrants, INTERPOL Red Notices, and the national administered sanctions lists; a risk-based enhanced due diligence review is required for any politically exposed person, and a negative screening certificate must be retained in the pre-incorporation file.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES – Registro Único Empresarial y Social (www.rues.org.co), administered by Confecámaras and local Cámaras de Comercio
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Proposed corporate names must be submitted in Spanish using Latin script; foreign words and trademark abbreviations are permissible only where descriptive of the business and transliterated into Spanish orthography; names must not be identical, confusingly similar, or phonetically identical to an existing registered company name or protected trade name in the same registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within 10 business days of a negative name clearance, the applicant may file a written reconsideration with the issuing Cámara de Comercio, providing evidence of phonetic uniqueness, prior consent from a registered name holder, or geographical and sectoral distinctiveness. If the chamber confirms rejection, an administrative appeal may be filed before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) under Articles 33 and 34 of the Código de Comercio. The original 60-day reservation is not extendable; after expiry or final rejection, a new name reservation request and payment of the applicable tariff must be submitted.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for an ISIC 4791 online retail operation provided a physical address in Colombia is designated for receiving official notifications and judicial service; a virtual office, law-firm address, or registered-agent office qualifies as the registered domicile, and no local warehouse or retail premises are required for desktop 3D printer, resin, and filament sales.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low; approximate 5-10% probability of an unannounced inspection within the first 24 months, increasing to 15-20% if DIAN, the Cámara de Comercio, or consumer-protection authorities receive complaints, logistics irregularities, or tax red flags. Standard e-commerce with no physical inventory is not a priority inspection target.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name search and homonymy certificate (Certificado de Homonimia)
Spanish drafting of S.A.S. private incorporation deed and articles of association (Documento Privado de Constitución, Estatutos)
Apostille, consular legalization, and authentication of foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Competent notarial or consular authority in the shareholder's jurisdiction

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified Spanish translation of foreign legal documents (parent certificate, board resolution, and powers of attorney)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Certified public translator or authorized translation bureau

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registration with the Cámara de Comercio and registration in RUES
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry tariff and registration tax

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation and first submission of the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF) declaration before DIAN
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: DIAN Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales and Colombian legal counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory compliance obligation with professional service fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate seal, minute book, share ledger, and accounting book legalization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Commercial notary or authorized corporate supplier

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada), arts. 1-12 and 45-46; Código de Comercio arts. 98-120 and 354 (supplementary); Decreto 1074 de 2015 (Ventanilla Única Empresarial); Superintendencia de Sociedades Resolution No. 200-000012 de 2022 (model S.A.S. bylaws)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá), under the administrative supervision of the Superintendencia de Sociedades
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation document) filed electronically through the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) for Matrícula Mercantil and issuance of the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital. At least twenty-five percent (25%) of the subscribed share capital must be paid in cash at incorporation (Ley 1258 de 2008, art. 12); the balance must be paid within two years. No escrow account is required; contributions in kind must be itemized and valued in the bylaws. Pending subscriptions do not prevent registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] S.A.S. RESOLVED: (1) The subscription of shares by the founding shareholders, as stated in the Private Incorporation Document, is hereby approved and ratified, and the paid-in portion equal to twenty-five percent (25%) of each share subscription is duly acknowledged. (2) The registered office is adopted at [Address], Bogotá D.C., Colombia, designated as the principal place of business and for all legal and tax notifications. (3) [Name] is appointed Legal Representative and [Name] as Acting Legal Representative, each with full power to execute registrations before the Chamber of Commerce, National Tax and Customs Directorate (DIAN), and banking authorities. (4) [Name] is appointed Secretary-Treasurer for fiscal administration. (5) All instruments required to effectuate these resolutions are ratified and approved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Pre-incorporation Name Availability and Homonymy Check
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá / local Chamber of Commerce via the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) online portal (www.vue.gov.co)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the Chamber's company registration module, submit up to three proposed company names, verify absence of an identical or confusingly similar registered name, obtain the Certificado de Homonimia, and reserve the preferred name for 30 days. The homonymy search covers the entire national commercial registry, preventing duplicate legal names.
required_dossiers: Cédula de ciudadanía / foreign ID of each founding shareholder
NIT or identification of acting legal representatives
Proposed company name (up to 3 alternatives in order of preference)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or queried for similarity, immediately submit a revised list of up to three alternative names; the Chamber re-runs the search within one business day at no additional fee. A 30-day reservation extension is available upon written request.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the Private Incorporation Document (Documento Privado de Constitución)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Corporate counsel / Notary Public (notarial certification optional for S.A.S.; recommended for evidentiary security); model bylaws published by the Superintendencia de Sociedades
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the estatutos strictly conforming to Ley 1258 de 2008 covering: company name, domicile, corporate purpose limited to ISIC 4791 online retail of desktop 3D printers and resin filaments, share capital and subscription schedule, 25% paid-in cash rule, administration rules, and powers of the Legal Representative. Execute the document with handwritten or electronic signatures of all subscribing shareholders, or proxy holders with valid power of attorney. Contributions in kind (if any) must be described and valued in the same instrument.
required_dossiers: Notarized power of attorney (if signing by proxy)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber identifies statutory deficiencies (e.g., omission of mandatory clauses per Ley 1258 arts. 4-10), prepare an amending document (documento de aclaración) reflecting corrections, re-execute before the same parties, and re-submit with the original application; the original filing date is normally preserved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Chamber of Commerce (Matrícula Mercantil and Issuance of Certificate of Existence)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the signed Documento Privado de Constitución via the VUE portal together with the official pre-registration form (Formulario Único de Registro). Pay the registration tariff (derechos de inscripción) electronically by PSE credit transfer. Upon approval, the Chamber issues the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, which constitutes conclusive evidence of incorporation and legal existence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected with a formal notice (auto de observaciones), correct the noted inconsistencies within 10 business days and resubmit electronically; curing within the deadline preserves the priority filing date and avoids refiling fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Taxpayer Registration — RUT and NIT before DIAN
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) — online portal www.dian.gov.co
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Access the DIAN electronic invoice and registration module using the company's NIT and the Legal Representative's electronic signature. Complete the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) application, selecting the applicable obligations: income tax (RENTA), VAT (IVA), national consumption tax if applicable, ICA municipal enrollment, and withholding agent duties (Retención en la Fuente). Obtain the official certified RUT copy, which authorizes the start of commercial invoicing.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (issued within 90 days)
Legal representative's cédula and electronic signature
Proof of registered office (lease or public services bill)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DIAN flags inconsistencies, correct the RUT electronically (Actualización RUT) and re-validate; for unresolved discrepancies, contact the DIAN tax information line (3078228 Bogotá) or visit the nearest DIAN service point; filing corrections do not suspend the NIT activation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Bank Account Opening (Operating and Payment Rails Account)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Commercial bank of choice (e.g., Bancolombia, BBVA Colombia, Davivienda)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the corporate package to the Bank's business division under the Simplified due diligence standard. Complete the AML/KYC/UBA (beneficial owner) questionnaire. The account must be linked to the target payment rails (Stripe, Shopify Payments) and will receive the paid-in capital contributions and e-commerce settlement funds. Banks typically require the certificate of existence to be issued within the last 30 days.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal (maximum age 30 days)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Bank requests additional UBO documentation, prepare a notarized Beneficial Owner Declaration (Formato UBO) and resubmit; if the review exceeds 10 business days, escalate to the Bank's commercial account manager or file a complaint with the Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia for undue delay.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Registrations: Commercial Books, Bylaw Enthronement, and Municipal ICA Enrollment
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social + Municipal / District Revenue Bureau (Secretaría Distrital de Hacienda) for ICA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within one month of incorporation, register the Libros de Comercio (journal, inventory, and minutes books — physical or digital per Código de Comercio arts. 50-63) at the Chamber of Commerce. Simultaneously, enroll the company in the municipal Registro de Actividades Económicas for the ICA tax (Industria y Comercio), obtaining the zonificación certificate (Certificado de Uso del Suelo) if a qualified warehouse space is used for resin storage.
required_dossiers: Board resolution appointing officers (unless stated in bylaws)
Libros de Comercio (physical or certified electronic evidence)
Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Zoning certificate for the warehouse/storage site (if applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the books are rejected for formal non-compliance, print new standardized books and reapply within 5 business days; if municipal zoning requires a compatible use certificate for light warehousing, obtain the Certificate of Compatible Land Use from the local planning authority (Curaduría Urbana) and resubmit.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial manufacturing in scope. Reference authority: Ministerio de Comercio, Industria y Turismo (MinCIT) through the Ventanilla Única Empresarial (VUE) for retail formalization; no sectoral operating permit is required for ISIC 4791 e-commerce retail of 3D printers and consumables.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required. Substituting agreements: Matrícula Mercantil, Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, RUT with ICA tax enrollment, and (if a physical warehouse is opened) the Certificado de Uso del Suelo (zoning certificate) issued by the municipal planning authority.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: ANLA — Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales for national projects; Corporación Autónoma Regional (CAR) for local warehouse sites under Decreto 1076 de 2015, Título VIII
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: EIA Exempt/Not Mandatory. Retail trade of 3D printers and filaments is not listed in the mandatory licensing catalogue. A full EIA is required only if the operator later develops an industrial production plant exceeding the capacity thresholds of Decree 1076/2015 or if a warehouse stores photopolymer resins above Category II hazardous-materials volumes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: If a warehouse or storage site operates: wastewater discharged to municipal sewers must comply with Resolución 0631 de 2015 (pH 6.0-9.0, TSS less than 60 mg/L, BOD5 less than 50 mg/L for new discharges); atmospheric emissions of Volatile Organic Compounds from resin storage are limited under Resolución 0909 de 2008 (VOC concentrations not exceeding 100 ppm at source); all photopolymer resin spills and expired materials must be managed as
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.residuo peligroso: per Decreto 4741 de 2005 with a hazardous waste manifest (EDS) and final disposal by a licensed transporter.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Cuerpo Oficial de Bomberos (Bomberos de Bogotá/local fire department) fire-safety inspection for any storage space: fire extinguishers, emergency signage, and evacuation routes; structural load compliance with the NSR-10 (Normas Sismorresistentes) for commercial/warehouse occupancy; Secretaría Distrital de Salud sanitary clearance for indoor storage of resin consumables; mandatory affiliation of all employees with an ARL (Administradora de Riesgos Laborales) and implementation of a workplace risk assessment and prevention plan per Resolución 0312 de 2019.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN). Primary digital portals: Muisca (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado) and 'Sí@' e-services on www.dian.gov.co; exporter and customs filing platforms: VUCE (Ventanilla Única de Comercio Exterior) and SIIS; corporate acts are registered with the Cámara de Comercio before DIAN tax enrollment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Procedure for a foreign-owned Colombian S.A.S.: (1) incorporate the S.A.S. by notarial deed or private instrument and register it with the Cámara de Comercio to obtain the certificate of existence and legal representation; (2) obtain the Registro Único Tributario (RUT) and the definitive 10-digit NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) through DIAN, either electronically on Muisca or at a DIAN service point; (3) complete the RUT with the ISIC 4791 e-commerce activity line and elect the status of 'responsable de IVA'; (4) enroll in the VUCE national exporters registry and secure the authorized digital signature for electronic export declarations; (5) activate mandatory electronic invoicing by obtaining an accredited digital signature certificate and requesting DIAN authorization for the Factura Electrónica de Venta, with the corresponding real-time pre-validation credentials; (6) where a foreign entity sells directly into Colombia without a Colombian entity, it must appoint a local apoderado and obtain its own NIT/RUT before commencing taxable sales.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The S.A.S. is a Colombian-resident juridical person subject to entity-level corporate income tax on worldwide income (35% general rate for tax year 2024; 20% inside an authorized Zona Franca only). It is not a pass-through for Colombian income tax purposes, and no Tax_Exempt_Zone status applies to this structure unless separately authorized. Territorial scope: Colombian residents have a worldwide tax base; non-resident sellers are taxed only on Colombian-source income.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Colombia has no U.S.-type check-the-box election. Relevant mechanisms: (i) optional election to apply the combined simplified regime 'Régimen Simple de Tributación (SIMPLE)' for eligible S.A.S. entities with prior-year gross income of not more than 100,000 UVT (approx. COP 4,706.5 million in 2024), substituting income tax and local trade tax with a single periodic turnover tax; (ii) voluntary registration as a VAT-responsible taxpayer by otherwise excludable small merchants (gross income under 3,500 UVT) to obtain input VAT credits; (iii) election for consolidated income tax filing by economic groups satisfying DIAN ownership and integration thresholds; (iv) anti-hybrid treatment: Colombian anti-deferral and mismatch rules under Law 1819/2016 and subsequent reforms generally respect the foreign jurisdiction's entity classification unless a deduction-without-inclusion or double-deduction outcome arises; no unilateral protective election form exists, and taxpayers must align documentation where Colombian and foreign classifications diverge.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (IVA - Impuesto sobre las Ventas), Estatuto Tributario Articles 420 et seq., compiled in Decreto Único Reglamentario 1625/2016.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary minimum triggers VAT responsibility: every supplier of taxable goods in Colombian territory, including a non-resident online retailer delivering 3D printers and consumables to Colombian consumers, must register in the RUT and charge IVA. The only statutory exclusion concerns small merchants whose gross income does not exceed 3,500 UVT (approx. COP 164,727,500 in 2024) and who are not importers or exporters; an e-commerce seller that imports or exports does not qualify for that exclusion and must be a full VAT-responsible taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing applies to all VAT-responsible taxpayers. The S.A.S. must issue the Factura Electrónica de Venta (FEV) in DIAN-approved XML/UBL format using accredited technology providers or certified in-house software; each invoice must pass DIAN 'Validación Previa' in real time and carry a unique CUNE (Código Único de Numeración) validation number (or issuer-generated CUFE in transitional modalities); digital signature certificates from DIAN-accredited certification authorities are mandatory; the payment rails (Stripe and Shopify Payments) must integrate with the DIAN-authorized invoicing flow to issue compliant FEV or consumer POS receipts. Export transactions are cross-controlled through the electronic Declaración de Exportación filed in VUCE/SIIS, with customs departure validation and automatic cross-matching of zero-rated export refund claims.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Physical exports of desktop 3D printers and resin filaments by the Colombian S.A.S. to foreign final customers qualify for 0% VAT as excluded sales with full right to input VAT credit/refund, provided: the exporter is registered in the RUT and the national exporters registry; the transaction is a definitive export under Decree 1165/2019; the goods physically depart Colombian customs territory within the applicable legal dispatch period; an electronic Declaración de Exportación is accepted by DIAN; export proceeds are repatriated through the Colombian foreign-exchange market within 180 days of the relevant shipment/declaration date; and contemporaneous documents prove order, payment, dispatch, and foreign receipt. Offshore services forming part of the hardware export may qualify under Estatuto Tributario Article 481 only if effectively used abroad; local delivery to Colombian addresses is never zero-rated.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) electronically lodged and accepted via VUCE/SIIS, identifying the DEX control number and DIAN customs validation
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or International Consignment Note proving physical departure of the goods from Colombian customs territory

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Comercialización de Divisas / foreign-exchange settlement statement) issued by an authorized Colombian FX intermediary, evidencing repatriation of the export sale proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN systematically cross-audits zero-rated export refunds against electronic invoicing, customs departure data, and FX settlement records. If the exporter fails to evidence a real, definitive export, the goods are not physically shipped, or the 180-day FX repatriation deadline is missed, the zero-rating is revoked and VAT becomes due on the invoice value, with moratory interest from the original filing date. Ancillary consequences include: the inexactness penalty under Estatuto Tributario Article 648 (100% of the tax difference, increased to 200% in abusive or artificially structured cases); the improper-refund penalty under Article 855 (restitution plus 100% of the amount improperly refunded); deregistration or suspension from the exporters registry; criminal tax-evasion or fraud prosecution under Law 1819/2016 as amended, carrying imprisonment of approximately 4 to 9 years and fines when the evaded or fraudulently refunded amount exceeds the statutory threshold; and joint liability of legal representatives, accountants, and board members who signed or certified the false returns.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia) as the monetary and exchange control authority, with the Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) enforcing customs and exchange infractions; regulatory framework comprises Law 9 of 1991, Decree 1068 of 2015 (Decreto Único Reglamentario del Sector Hacienda), Circular Reglamentaria DCIN-83 (foreign exchange regulations), and the Foreign Investment Statistical Registration regime administered by Banco de la República.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia maintains a managed floating exchange regime with a fully regulated 'mercado cambiario' (foreign exchange market). Current account transactions (goods imports, services, royalties, and profit remittances derived from registered investment) are freely convertible and channeled through authorized intermediaries without prior central bank approval. Capital account transactions, including inbound direct investment, must be registered with Banco de la República to legitimize the right to remit dividends, capital gains, and repatriate principal. Colombia retains a 10% remittance tax (impuesto de remesas) on net after-tax profits remitted to non-resident shareholders, without treaty reduction; the SAS must therefore document that Ecuador/EU/Other treaty sourcing does not otherwise alter local remittance taxation. FX convertibility for e-commerce collections from Stripe/Shopify is operationally straightforward, subject to correct purpose-code classification and monthly/quarterly filing of the Declaración de Cambio through a local bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds from goods (3D printers, resin filaments, consumables) must be channeled through the Colombian foreign exchange market via an authorized local intermediary within six (6) months from the date of shipment, extendable by up to an additional six (6) months upon justified request to Banco de la República. There is no compulsory surrender/conversion quota to the Central Bank; the exporter may hold the foreign currency in a local foreign-currency checking account ('cuenta de compensación') or a foreign overseas account, but the proceeds must still be registered through the 'Declaración de Cambio' (form code 3101 for goods exports) and must remain identifiable against the export customs declaration (exportación). Services and digital platform remuneration must be channeled within six (6) months from the accrual date. Failure to channel within the statutory term constitutes an exchange infraction under Article 5 of Law 9 of 1991, punishable by fines calculated on the unpaid or late-regulated amount.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Capitalización) and Operational Account (COP and USD denominated)
Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente COP/USD) with dedicated sub-account for FX channeling declarations
Operational Account and Foreign Investment Settlement Sub-Account
Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente USD and COP) with integrated digital FX platform
Operational Account for trade settlement and documentary collections
Operational Account paired with international cash management services

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-High as a supplementary collection/disbursement rail, but never a statutory substitute for a local bank account. Foreign EMIs (e.g., Stripe, PayPal, Payoneer, Wise, Airwallex) are not licensed credit institutions under Colombian law; they operate as foreign payment service providers and their accounts are classified as 'cuentas en el exterior' for regulatory purposes. They are viable for aggregating card-based e-commerce receipts from buyers in Latin America and for low-value supplier disbursements, but the SAS must (i) maintain a local authorized-intermediary account to channel regulated FX transactions, (ii) file Formulario No. 13 (reporte de cuentas en el exterior) with Banco de la República for any overseas account whose monthly balance exceeds USD 12,000, and (iii) incorporate the third-party settlement flows into the Declaración de Cambio as services or goods receipts. Legal constraints include lack of DIAN-backed receipts for VAT/ICA purposes, potential commission erosion, and the impossibility of obtaining an export channeling certificate directly from an EMI.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the general rule for the legal representative and ultimate beneficial owners; Colombian anti-money-laundering Circular 060 of 2023 and bank underwriting policies require a notarized and chamber-verified identity verification ('certificado de cámara y comercio') together with in-branch or video-assisted interview for non-face-to-face onboarding. Most tier-1 banks (Bancolombia, BBVA, Davivienda) permit a qualified remote-onboarding flow for low-risk e-commerce SAS entities using video identification, digital signature, and certified RUT validation; yet the majority expect at least one in-person visit by the legal representative in Bogotá/Medellín within the first six months. A fully remote alternative is available by granting a 'poder especial' to a local legal representative or CPA, apostilled under the Hague Convention and legalized by the Colombian consulate if the origin country is not an apostille member; the power must explicitly authorize opening accounts, signing FX declarations, and filing foreign investment registrations. In practice, budget for one physical trip at onboarding and annual compliance reviews.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: high-frequency cross-border e-commerce receivables from fragmented, unrelated customer base with no established correspondent banking relationship and large card-present/settlement volatility.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Compliance bundle must include: (i) executed platform agreements with Stripe and Shopify Payments evidencing the transaction engine and settlement terms; (ii) standardized customer order records, export waybills, and carrier shipping documents (DHL, FedEx) demonstrating physical inventory flow; (iii) Colombian VAT and income tax filings (declaraciones de IVA y renta) reconciled to reported revenue; (iv) Chamber of Commerce certificate of existence and legal representation; (v) commercial contracts with filament/resin manufacturers proving sourcing; (vi) a written source-of-funds and business-model narrative classifying the entity as Low_Risk_Standard maker-hardware e-commerce under AML Circular 060.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Shareholder/UBO opacity: non-resident ownership structure with intermediate holding vehicles or shareholders domiciled in high-risk/high-tax jurisdictions without a clear economic rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver: (i) apostilled certificate of incorporation and register of ultimate beneficial owners ('acta de beneficiario final'); (ii) individual UBO declarations with notarized passport copies; (iii) foreign tax residency certificates (certificado de residencia fiscal) for each direct shareholder; (iv) completed PEP (politically exposed person) questionnaire for every beneficial owner and immediate family members; (v) corporate organization chart with full ownership percentages and an economic-substance justification for the Colombian SAS; (vi) sworn statement affirming the absence of shell or nominee arrangements, backed by audited financial statements where available.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sudden spike in outbound wire disbursements to high-risk supplier jurisdictions (e.g., China, Hong Kong SAR, Singapore) for 3D printer consumables that could appear as trade-based money laundering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (i) purchase orders, proforma invoices, and master supply agreements with original equipment manufacturers; (ii) logistics contracts and bill-of-lading/AWB evidence for each cleared shipment; (iii) corresponding customer sales orders proving commercial end-use; (iv) a periodic counterparty AML screening policy and screening reports against OFAC/EU/Colombia lists; (v) FX declaration forms (Declaración de Cambio codes 3301/3101) aligned with the import/export customs operations; (vi) explainable transfer-pricing benchmark or arm's-length margin documentation demonstrating that the trade prices match market values for filaments and consumables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient capital-contribution traceability when the SAS receives shareholder funds as 'loans' instead of registered equity, triggering misclassification under foreign investment rules.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare: (i) executed shareholder loan or subscription agreement with currency, amount, and repayment schedule; (ii) SWIFT MT103 records showing the exact inbound transfer and remitter identity; (iii) Formulario No. 5 (Registro de Inversiones Internacionales) filed within 12 months of disbursement, clearly coded as equity ('inversión directa') or external credit; (iv) board resolutions (actas) approving the capital injection; (v) bank statement of the capital escrow account proving the funds were not immediately withdrawn; (vi) a written opinion or checklist confirming that the transaction complies with Circular DCIN-83 and triggers the correct Declaración de Cambio code.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident shareholders must remit equity contributions via SWIFT MT103 to the SAS's dedicated USD or COP account at a local authorized intermediary, using the standard purpose code for direct investment (3201 - 'Inversión de capital') in the 'Declaración de Cambio por Inversiones Internacionales'. The foreign investment must be registered with Banco de la República using Formulario No. 5 within twelve (12) months of disbursement; registration is a precondition to the lawful remittance of dividends and repatriation of capital. Funds should be isolated in a capital escrow sub-account to maintain an unbroken audit trail. For working-capital loans from the parent or third party, the routing uses external credit codes 3602/3603, and if the maturity exceeds one year, the credit must be registered as 'crédito externo' with the Central Bank. All inbound wires must match the beneficiary legal name as it appears on the RUT and bank account mandate; the bank will generate the mandatory 'Declaración de Cambio' and the compliance department should store the SWIFT reference, purpose code, and underlying investment registration receipt.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for 3D printer inventory and consumables use the following rails through the local authorized intermediary: (i) SWIFT MT103 remittances for low-value recurring supplier invoices (filaments, resins, print heads), each supported by a Declaración de Cambio with goods import code 3301 and the corresponding customs import declaration; (ii) commercial letters of credit (sight or deferred LC) for bulk procurement from overseas manufacturers, with payment in USD against shipping documents (negotiable bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, certificate of origin), providing seller assurance and bank-verified compliance; (iii) documentary collections (D/P or D/A) for medium-risk suppliers; and (iv) escrowed payment mechanisms for marketplace vendor settlements. Every outbound disbursement requires reconciliation with the local inventory import records and the SAP/ERP purchase ledger; DIAN and Banco de la República expect the underlying import declaration to be filed within 15 days of the customs broker filing, and FX channeling to be completed within the statutory timeline for import payments to avoid exchange infractions.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Spot foreign currency purchase/sale against COP through authorized intermediaries
Deliverable forward contracts (compra/venta a término) with licensed local banks, collateralized under ISDA/CMVM mandates
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on USD/COP executed with authorized local counterparties or registered foreign banks under Banco de la República rules
Cross-currency swaps (swaps de moneda) between COP and USD with locally authorized financial institutions
Foreign exchange options (opciones cambiarias) and participating forwards ('forwards participativos') traded over the counter through regulated intermediaries

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual commercial registry renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio of the registered seat (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March of each calendar year; no extension period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers an SMMLV-indexed surcharge and interest; certificate issuances are withheld; after 3 continuous years of non-renewal the commercial registry may be cancelled and the company struck off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approved annual financial statements and management report of the Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (filed as supporting documentation to the annual renewal); approval by shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Shareholders' meeting must approve the prior fiscal year's financial statements no later than 31 March; filing accompanies the commercial registry renewal by the same deadline
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve and file financial statements is a statutory default subject to commercial fines; the legal representative may face administrative liability, and the company's renewal status may be placed in non-compliant status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficiiarios finales confirmation (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in the first half-year, with specific due date set by NIT last digit and usually falling between March and 31 May
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or inaccurate reporting gives rise to monetary sanctions under Colombian tax law, potential suspension of RUT status, and administrative penalties against the legal representative.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Revisor Fiscal (statutory auditor) is mandatory if total assets exceed 5,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 1.8 million) or gross operating income exceeds 3,000 SMMLV (approx. USD 1.1 million), or if the company is permanently supervised by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian local GAAP based on IFRS; the S.A.S. applies NIIF para Pymes (IFRS for SMEs) under Decreto 2420 de 2015 unless it qualifies as a larger Grupo 1 entity.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must report all direct and indirect shareholders owning 20% or more, and any natural persons exercising control, through the DIAN Beneficiarios Finales module. An annual confirmation is filed each calendar year irrespective of changes; any share transfer or ownership variation during the year must be reflected in the year-end UBO filing.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors / Minutes of Board or Sole Director (Libro de Actas)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - 700 (virtual office in Bogotá or Medellín)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500 - 6,000 (when Revisor Fiscal is mandatory; USD 800 - 1,500 for unaudited review-only financial statements)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory holiday. The standard rate for S.A.S. entities is 35% (Art. 240 of the Colombian Tax Statute). Targeted deductions may lower the effective rate, e.g., 25% deduction for R&D investment (Art. 158-1 ET), 50% deduction for investments in environmental control and improvement (Art. 255 ET), and 100% deduction for new productive fixed assets purchased in the current year (Art. 158-2 ET). For an e-commerce reseller with no special regime, the effective rate most commonly equals the statutory 35%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 210 - Declaración de Renta y Complementarios para Personas Jurídicas y Asimiladas; filed electronically via DIAN's MUISCA platform (https://dian.gov.co).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual return must be filed and paid by the 9th day of the ninth month (usually September 9) of the fiscal year subsequent to the taxable period. The exact date is determined by the last two digits of the tax identification number (NIT) and set by DIAN Resolution each year (e.g., NIT ending 01-10: September 9; 11-20: September 10; 21-30: September 11; 31-40: September 12; 41-50: September 13; 51-60: September 14; 61-70: September 15; 71-80: September 16; 81-90: September 17; 91-99: September 18).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxpayer identification number (NIT) of the S.A.S.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Not applicable – the entity is a Colombian resident corporation. Foreign shareholders do not directly file this return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross income from online sales and other ordinary activities (including all e-commerce revenue recognized as Colombian-source income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include global income attributable to the Colombian entity under the worldwide residence principle; foreign income may be exempt if subject to the territoriality rules, but online retail revenue is typically Colombian-source.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Returns, rebates and discounts recognized in the fiscal period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report non-resident adjustments only if directly attributable to the Colombian entity's commercial operations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total costs and deductions (purchases of 3D printers, filaments, shipping, software, advertising, salaries, depreciation).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deduct expenses incurred abroad only if supported by proper documentation and used in the production of Colombian-source income; transfer pricing limits may apply.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income before tax credits (liquid taxable income).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Computed after applying allowed tax losses carryforward (12-year limit).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income tax expense at the standard 35% rate (Box 64 × 35%).
Total tax payable after deduction of tax prepayments, withholding credits and industrial allowance.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the S.A.S. is 100% foreign-owned, any foreign tax credits must be claimed on the Colombian return only if a tax treaty provides for such crediting.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual return attracts a fine of up to 5% of the tax due for each month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% of the tax due. If no tax is due, a fixed fine of up to 1,560 UVT (approx. COP 73,400,000 for 2024) applies. Late payment interest accrues at the current official rate (approx. 1.5% monthly) plus applicable surcharges. In addition, failure to file under the information return regime can trigger a fine of 1% of the commercial value, not less than 10 UVT and not more than 5,000 UVT.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced rate for dividends, royalties, or interest under a double taxation agreement (DTA), the foreign beneficiary must provide to the Colombian withholding agent (the Colombian S.A.S.) a valid Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) issued by the foreign tax authority. The TRC must be apostilled or legalised as required, and must be filed with DIAN via the MUISCA system, generally through the withholding agent's periodic withholding returns. The Colombian payor must keep the TRC in its files and report the payment on Form 140 (information return on payments abroad). If the TRC is not provided before the payment due date, the statutory 10% dividend withholding (and 15% for royalties/interest) must be withheld, and a revised refund or credit can be sought only through a DIAN tax refund process or relief under the applicable DTA.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates for non-resident recipients: 15% withholding on royalties from the use of patents, know-how, trademarks, or similar IP (Art. 408 ET) and 15% withholding on interest and financial income (Art. 408 ET). Under certain DTAs (e.g., Mexico, Spain, Switzerland, Chile, Portugal, and Korea) royalty rates may be reduced to 10% or 5%, and interest rates to 10% or 5% depending on the treaty.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Documentation is mandatory for taxpayers whose gross assets or gross income as of the prior fiscal year equals or exceeds 100,000 UVT (COP 4,706,500,000 for taxable year 2024). The multinational group's Master File and Country-by-Country report are required when consolidated group revenue exceeds COP 1,247,000 million (approx. USD 350 million) or the equivalent of EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not have a formal Economic Substance Regulation (ESR) akin to the Gulf jurisdictions. However, subjective substance requirements are embedded in Article 868-1 ET (transactions without economic substance may be disregarded) and Article 869 ET (general anti-avoidance rule – GAAR). In practice, DIAN expects a Colombian S.A.S. to demonstrate a physical presence (office, warehouse, employees), real operational decision-making, and sufficient business functions related to e-commerce sales. If the entity is deemed to be a shell or captive intermediary, DIAN may recharacterise the transactions, deny deductions, and hold the directors jointly liable for the resulting tax deficiency.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately underreporting online sales revenue; generating false e-commerce invoices; repeated omission of VAT collection or evasion of income tax through manipulation of transaction records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 1819 of 2016 (Art. 33, Colombian Criminal Code), tax evasion is a criminal offence punishable by imprisonment of 48 to 108 months (4 to 9 years), fines equivalent to 200% of the evaded tax, and disqualification from contracting with the State for up to 10 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and legal representatives who knowingly participate in the evasion face criminal liability, civil restitution obligations, asset seizure, and a travel ban pending investigation. The corporate veil can be pierced under Article 372 of the Commercial Code, rendering directors jointly liable for the company's tax debts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the S.A.S. as a paper company without physical premises, employees, operational records, or commercial substance; issuing invoices for purchases or sales without actual logistics or inventory movement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disregard the legal entity under Article 868-1 ET, subjecting the entire taxable income to immediate taxation. Penalties can reach up to 200% of the improperly avoided tax (Law 1943 of 2018, Art. 99). Alternatively, the company may be voided and liquidated as a fictitious entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign or silently benefit from sham transactions may be jointly and severally liable for all tax, fines and interest; they can also be subjected to commercial disqualification and criminal prosecution for conspiracy to commit fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting cash or cryptocurrency payments for high-volume 3D printer sales without implementing Anti-Money Laundering (AML) controls; failure to file transaction reports with UIAF (Unidad de Información y Análisis Financiero) when payments exceed 1,000 UVT; using Stripe or Shopify to launder illicit funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Law 1121 of 2006 and Article 323 of the Criminal Code (as amended by Law 1762 of 2015), money laundering is punishable by imprisonment of 6 to 15 years and fines of up to 50,000 S.M.M.L.V. (monthly minimum legal salary); administrative sanctions from UIAF can include monetary fines up to COP 1 billion and suspension of the company's commercial activities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, compliance officers, and beneficial owners are criminally liable for negligent AML compliance. Personal assets can be seized, and directors may be subject to a travel ban and imprisonment; under the corporate veil, courts may impose direct liability for reparations.
